confirmed.title: settle() gravitational-drag loss uses the wrong units (x v^2 instead of x v): per-trip energy ~3,700x too big, settling time ~17x too short
confirmed.claim: In settle()/passFor the gravitational-drag term is m*dfCoef(m,rho,v)*v2*dr. dfCoef is F/(m v) (units 1/s), so m*dfCoef*v^2 is force times speed (W), and multiplying by dr gives W*m, not J. The drag force is m*dfCoef*v. fallThrough (line 803) and gravDragDominant (line 941) both use it correctly. The bug overstates the loss per trip by a factor of v (~4,000 m/s). Every heavy body therefore 'settles' in the same ~126 years: 7.4e16 kg and 1e18 kg both give 125.86 yr, which gives the bug away. The Weight tab's headline settle tile, its range, the per-trip TNT figure and the quake magnitude are all wrong for neutron-star-class Rex.
confirmed.evidence: node: P.settle(P.makeBody({H:2,m:7.416e16})) -> firstPassLossJ 1.553e22 J, years 125.9; with {sigma:4.1e9,k:2} 81.0 yr. The same engine's 3-D P.fallThrough gives firstPass.depthShort 5.27 m, i.e. m*g*5.27 = 3.84e18 J lost per trip. An independent 1-D through-centre integration (my own PREM mass integral, sigma 1.7 GPa, k=1, Ostriker I(M) with c_s 6 km/s, lnL 5) gives 4.18e18 J per trip, turns back 5.8 m short, 2,291 s. A scratch copy patched to '* v' gives firstPassLossJ 4.18e18 J and 2,198 yr (strong-rock end 1,395 yr, weak end 29,065 yr unchanged). Page state {"group":"solo","action":"weight","m":7.416e16} shows 'Settles at the centre after ~130 years / anywhere from 81 years to 29,000 years' and 'costs him about 3.7 x 10^12 t TNT per trip (... magnitude 8.9 quake)'. Expected: ~2,200 yr (about 1,400-29,000), ~1.0 x 10^9 t TNT per trip, magnitude ~6.5. At m=1e18 the page shows 6.7e14 t TNT per trip, M10 and ~130 yr; patched gives 3.3e20 J (M7.8) and 512 yr.
confirmed.fix: Line 874: replace `m * dfCoef(m, rho, v) * v2` with `m * dfCoef(m, rho, v) * v`. Add a calibration check that settle().firstPassLossJ matches m*g*fallThrough().firstPass.depthShort within ~15% for the neutron-star preset.

verdict.title: settle() gravitational-drag loss uses the wrong units (x v^2 instead of x v): per-trip energy ~3,700x too big, settling time ~17x too short
verdict.reason: Reproduced. Line 886 (the finder said 874) adds m*dfCoef*v2 to a sum of forces (A*sigma, A*k*rho*v^2), so that term is force times speed. At H=2 m, m=7.416e16, the original gives firstPassLossJ 1.553e22 J and 125.9 yr. My scratch copy patched to '* v' gives 4.183e18 J and 2,198 yr. Both 7.4e16 and 1e18 kg give the same 125.9 yr in the original. fallThrough's own depthShort gives m*g*5.27 m = 3.83e18 J, which matches the patched value to 9%. At the current 3.05 m default, the page for m=7.416e16 says '~82 years / 53 years to 13,000 years' and '3.7 x 10^12 t TNT per trip ... magnitude 8.9 quake'. Patched, that becomes ~1,350 yr (757 to 12,500 yr), 1.75e9 t TNT and M6.7. The same paragraph also says he comes back up 7.06-17.1 m short, which is ~7e18 J, so the page contradicts itself. Not covered by the density critique, which asked for gravitational drag to be added, not for this units slip.
verdict.fix: In passFor, use m * dfCoef(m, rho, v) * v (the force), not * v2. Add a calibration check that settle().firstPassLossJ is within ~15% of m*g*fallThrough().firstPass.depthShort for the neutron-star preset, and that the settle years differ between 7.4e16 and 1e18 kg.

confirmed.title: Relativistic catch leaves out the energy that reaches the catcher; the blast uses only the snowplow heat, and it shrinks as Ollie stands closer
confirmed.claim: For the 'arrives' and 'plasma' kinds, the page reports only Egap and feeds only Egap to the blast block, labelled 'Upper bound'. Egap is the lump's invariant-mass increase. The lump still carries Earr = E - Egap (nearly all of E) into Ollie. When bolted Ollie stops it, the Earth takes p^2/2M_E (negligible), so almost all of E is released where he stands. In the snowplow model the heat also rides inside the lump, so nothing is 'left in the gap'. The reported blast therefore falls as Ollie moves closer, although the same energy is released by him at every distance. The Collide tab does this correctly (Elocal = KA + air above 1% of c).
confirmed.evidence: node: P.catchLeg(bolted ctx F=1e22*g, bolted ctx F=1e22*g, car, D, 'hard').fireball. D=10 m: kind 'arrives', E 5.25e22 J, Egap 7.45e20 J; the blast uses 7.45e20 J (windows-shatter radius 756 km). D=1 km: 'plasma', Egap 8.99e21 J (1,735 km). D=14.5 km: 'before', blast uses E 5.25e22 J (3,123 km). Page state {"group":"duo","duoAction":"catch","cObj":"car","cStyle":"hard","logKg":22,"anchor":"bolted","oAnchor":"bolted"} says 'The air between them takes 745 EJ ... as heat, right next to them' and 'Upper bound'. Pyramid (logKg 30; the page clamps D to ~71 m) shows 3.6e25 J, 'roughly 90x the dinosaur-killing asteroid'. The pyramid's E = 5.28e30 J, 2.1% of Earth's binding energy; Earth's recoil energy from p = 1.76e22 is only 2.6e19 J.
confirmed.fix: For 'arrives' and 'plasma', report the energy released at the catcher as E: minus p^2/2M_E if bolted, or carried on with him if free (the snowplow then dumps it within the sweep length). Feed E to blastBlock. Describe Egap as 'already heat when it reaches him', not 'left in the gap'. Never call the Egap blast an upper bound. Add a test that the blast energy does not decrease as D decreases.

verdict.title: Relativistic catch leaves out the energy that reaches the catcher; the blast uses only the snowplow heat, and it shrinks as Ollie stands closer
verdict.reason: Reproduced. For the car at a 1e22 dial with both bolted (3.05 m/637 kg bodies), E = 7.88e22 J at every distance. The blast energy fed to blastBlock is Egap: 8.8e20 J at 10 m, 3.6e21 at 100 m, 1.1e22 at 1 km, 3.5e22 at 14.5 km. It then jumps to E = 7.9e22 J at 30 km ('before'). So the reported blast grows as Ollie moves away. For the pyramid at 10 m, Egap is 5.7e22 J while E = 8.0e30 J. The page shows 5.4e25 J ('roughly 100x the dinosaur-killing asteroid') and labels it 'Upper bound'. The lump still carries Earr (about E) into bolted Ollie, and Earth's recoil energy is p^2/2M_E (5.8e3 J for the car, 6e19 J for the pyramid). So nearly all of E is released where he stands. The 'arrives' verdict never states that energy. The catch critique (item 2) asked for the momentum push only and never dealt with this energy, so this is not a repeat.
verdict.fix: For 'arrives' and 'plasma', report energy released at or just past the catcher as E minus p^2/(2 M_E) when bolted. When he is free, he and the lump ride on and dump it within about one sweep length. Feed that to blastBlock and quake. Describe Egap as heat already made on the way, not the whole release. Don't call this blast an upper bound. Add a test that blast energy never decreases as D decreases.

confirmed.title: Arm wrestling 'pins' a loser whose arm is far stronger than his footing (and the winner can be the weaker arm)
confirmed.claim: After the table breaks, or when the winner is bolted, AA and AB are capped by footing, and the loser's footing is passed to pushApart as RB. The model then folds the loser's forearm (3.5-4.7 kg effective) against his foot friction. If the loser's arm is stronger than his feet, though, his arm never yields: the hand force can't exceed the winner's footing, so the loser's whole body slides instead. The pin time, hand speed and slam energy are then fiction, and the 'winner' can have the weaker arm. The verdict text is also self-contradictory. Separately, when the table holds and the surplus is huge, the pin needs elbow-pad reactions far above the table's stated capacity.
confirmed.evidence: node: P.armWrestle(Rex F=1e12 kg*g 180 kg, Ollie F=1e11 kg*g 300 kg) gives PA 2.45e12 N, PB 2.45e11 N, tableBreaks, AA 1,059 N, AB 1,765 N, outcome 'pin', winner B, t 88.7 ms, v 13.5 m/s, E 421 J. Page {"group":"duo","duoAction":"arm","logKg":12,"oSame":false,"oLogKg":11,"oM":300} says 'Ollie wins by only 706 N ... He pins Rex in 89 ms. The back of Rex's hand hits the pad at 13.5 m/s, cracking the top.' A <=1.77 kN hand force cannot fold a 2.45 TN arm. Expected: no pin; Rex's body slides under 706 N net (3.9 m/s^2 on 180 kg). Page {"group":"duo","duoAction":"arm","anchor":"bolted"} says 'The table breaks first ... Rex wins by only 221 kN because his feet hold ∞ N ... He pins Ollie in 4.3 ms. The back of Ollie's hand hits the pad at 275 m/s and goes through the table.' Ollie's 222 kN arm can't be folded through his 1.06 kN feet; his body is dragged instead (~38 m/s). Table-holds case ({"oSame":false,"oLogKg":2.7084}): the 221 kN surplus gives 63,400 m/s^2 at the grip. The 7.92 kg of forearms, with their centre of mass at 0.208/0.38 of the lever, then need ~275 kN sideways at the elbow pads, 42x the 6.48 kN the page says the table carries.
confirmed.fix: When the loser's binding limit is his footing (P_loser > R_loser), the outcome is a drag or slide of the loser's whole body (mass m plus arms, net Aw - R_loser), not a pin. Pin only when the loser's arm force is the limit. Fix the bolted-winner verdict template ('his feet hold ∞ N') and the wording 'table breaks first ... goes through the table'. When the table holds, compare the peak sideways pad load (forearm mass x a_cm) with tableLat.

verdict.title: Arm wrestling 'pins' a loser whose arm is far stronger than his footing (and the winner can be the weaker arm)
verdict.reason: Reproduced. armWrestle(Rex 1e12 kg dial, 300 kg; Ollie 1e11 kg dial, 637 kg) gives a pin by B: Ollie, with a 2.45e11 N arm, pins Rex's 2.45e12 N arm in 91 ms at 19.9 m/s, only because Ollie's feet hold more. With unequal dials (oSame reset removed in a scratch copy of the page), the page says 'He pins Ollie in 91 ms' about an Ollie whose arm is 245 GN while Rex's hand force is at most 3.75 kN. It also shows the chip 'Ollie's feet slip above 1.77 kN'. Folding the loser's forearm needs a hand force above his arm strength, which the winner's footing can't supply. Under the page's own premise ('each can only press as hard as his feet hold'), the loser's whole body slides. The bolted default ({anchor:'bolted'}) prints 'Rex wins by only 219 kN because his feet hold ∞ N, not his full 222 kN' and '...goes through the table' after 'The table breaks first'. The contest critique's test correction 5 asked for exactly this feet-only pin, so the finding challenges an applied fix whose physics is wrong, which is allowed. The table-holds sub-claim is right as an estimate. The forearms (0.022 m each, centre of mass at 0.547 of the lever) need about 270 kN of elbow reaction, against the table's 15.1 kN. The page partly covers it with 'Pin smashes the table'.
verdict.fix: After the table breaks, if the loser's arm force exceeds the hand force the winner can apply (P_loser > min(P_winner, R_winner)), there is no pin. Report the loser's whole body being dragged or shoved sideways (mass m plus arms, net = applied hand force - R_loser) and drop the pin/slam/hand-speed tiles. Pin only when the loser's arm force is the binding limit. Fix the bolted-winner template ('his feet hold ∞ N') and the 'breaks first ... through the table' wording. When the table holds, compare the peak sideways elbow load (forearm mass x a_cm) with tableLat.

confirmed.title: Catch survival gate ignores the first-contact force, so a shot put crushed on contact is 'caught' (and the throw push is never checked)
confirmed.claim: wholeFront uses only Fobj, the arm-stroke force. For objects about as light as his hands, the first-contact force F1 (which the same function computes) is 20-30x larger and on its own exceeds the object's crush strength spread over its whole front. The page then says 'caught' and advises a plate larger than the object's own front, which can't spread the load. The throw side has no matching check: Rex's push on the object can exceed crush strength over its front before it leaves his hand.
confirmed.evidence: node: P.catchLeg(bolted F=1e7*g, bolted F=1e7*g, shot, 10, 'hard') gives result 'caught'. F1 = 1.76e8-4.39e8 N; front 0.0113 m^2; crush 7.5e8 Pa. F1_low/area = 1.56e10 Pa, 20.8x crush, while the engine's wholeFront is 0.757. Page {"group":"duo","duoAction":"catch","cObj":"shot","cStyle":"hard","logKg":7,"anchor":"bolted","oAnchor":"bolted"} says 'Stops it; his palms punch in ... To catch it whole he'd need a plate 48 cm x 48 cm'; the shot's front is ~10.6 cm square. Throw push on the shot is m vL^2/(2 x 1.6 m) = 7.26 x 2169^2/3.2 = 1.07e7 N, 1.26x crush over its front. A sweep (objects with crush x dial 1e5-1e9 x D 10/100/1000 m x lob/fastball x friction/bolted) gives 276 'caught' verdicts; 10 of them (shot put, dial 1e6-1e7) fail on first contact.
confirmed.fix: Use wholeFront = max(F1[0], Fobj)/area/crush, and treat plateNeeded > obj.area as 'wreckage'. Add the throw-side check: if the object's push divided by its area exceeds crush, it is crushed in the thrower's hands (break-up at launch).

verdict.title: Catch survival gate ignores the first-contact force, so a shot put crushed on contact is 'caught' (and the throw push is never checked)
verdict.reason: Reproduced. Line 2282 sets wholeFront = Fobj/area/crush, and line 2430 gates 'wreckage' on it, but F1 (first contact) is 20-200x larger for light objects. At a 1e7 dial, bolted, 10 m fastball: F1 = 1.41e8-3.53e8 N on a 0.0113 m^2 front gives 12.5 GPa, 16.7x the 750 MPa crush, while wholeFront is 0.074. The page says 'Stops it; his palms punch in ... To catch it whole he'd need a plate 43 cm x 43 cm', a plate far bigger than the ~10.6 cm shot, which can't spread the load. My sweep of crushable objects (dial 1e3-1e12 x D 10/100/1000 x easy/hard x friction/bolted) gives 591 'caught' verdicts. 21 fail on first contact over the whole front: the shot put at dials 1e6-1e8 (up to 166x crush), plus the motorcycle and the piano. The catch critique's gate (c) was implemented with the arm-stroke force only, so this fix is incomplete. The throw-side push is marginal at 1e7 (~1.0x crush with a 1.6 m stroke) and grows with the dial. It is a valid secondary point.
verdict.fix: Use wholeFront = max(F1[0], Fobj)/obj.area/obj.crush, and treat plateNeeded > obj.area as 'wreckage' (no plate helps). Add a launch check: if the throwing push over the object's front exceeds its crush strength, it is crushed in the thrower's hand.

verdict.title: Unlimited momentum into bolted Rex on real rock: verdict says the rock gives, tiles say the Earth takes it at exactly 3 x 10^8 m/s
verdict.reason: Reproduced on the page ({group:'duo',duoAction:'collide',colSrc:'set',colInf:true,anchor:'bolted'}). The verdict says 'Rex is torn loose with a plug of rock and knocked away at just under light speed'. The same page shows the chip 'Bolted: Earth takes the blow', 'Rock cracks ∞ around his bolts', the tile 'Earth's speed change 3 x 10^8 m/s / it would take 0.0033 ns to move 1 mm', and the text 'The Earth takes the momentum ... his momentum stays with the Earth'. confirmed.title: Catch stroke time is capped in a way that breaks impulse = change in momentum, and the round trip uses it
confirmed.claim: tStroke is capped at 2d/v, where v is the speed before contact. After first contact, though, the ball and hands move at v1 = v m/(m+mh), and the stated arm force F was chosen to stop them over d. For light objects the capped time is far shorter than F allows, so F*t is much smaller than the momentum removed. The page states both the force and the time, and they contradict each other.
confirmed.evidence: Default lob {"group":"duo","duoAction":"catch"}: F = 1.2 N on m+mh = 8.065 kg at v1 = 0.161 m/s (p = 1.30 N*s; the net decelerating force after gravity along the line is 0.175 N). That needs 2d/v1 = 7.45 s, but the engine uses tStroke 0.134 s (impulse 0.16 N*s). The page shows round trip 'about 3.87 s'. With the stated 1.2 N it would be ~18.5 s; keeping 0.134 s needs ~10.7 N. Fastball: tStroke 2.2 ms at 651 N against (m+mh)v1 = 79 N*s (needs ~0.12 s).
confirmed.fix: Use tStroke = vE/aRel, which matches F. Alternatively, pick a stroke time and recompute F = Δp/t plus the gravity term. Don't combine the two.

verdict.title: Catch stroke time is capped in a way that breaks impulse = change in momentum, and the round trip uses it
verdict.reason: Reproduced at the current defaults (3.05 m bodies, 28 kg of hands). For the default lob, v1 = 0.0442 m/s, so (m+m_h)v1 = 1.245 N*s. The page says 'His arms then bring it in over 91 cm with 1.05 N', yet tStroke = 2d/v = 0.214 s (F*t = 0.225 N*s). At the stated force the stroke takes ~41 s (2d/v1), against the 'Round trip about 4.45 s' shown. Fastball: 63.9 N with tStroke 4.6 ms against 57.4 N*s, which needs ~0.9 s. The two shown numbers disagree. A careful reader could catch it, but it doesn't change any verdict.
verdict.fix: Choose a stroke time (e.g. 2d/vE, or a capped human-like time) and recompute F = Δp/t + gravity term from it, or show the round trip with tStroke = vE/aRel. Never pair a minimum force with a time it can't produce.

confirmed.title: 'Reshapes' regime still shows 'Earth falls onto him in 14.9 min' and an overstated energy floor
confirmed.claim: For M_RESHAPE <= m < M_E the tile says 'Earth falls onto him in ... free fall from the surface'. tff is the pressureless collapse time of the whole Earth onto m + M_E, which doesn't happen at 0.17% of Earth's mass; the verdict correctly says he sinks to the centre. An earlier critique asked for this to be dropped; only the verdict was changed. The 'at least' energy uses G m M_E/R_E (6.26e7 J/kg), but the guaranteed part, sinking from the surface to the centre in PREM, is 4.92e7 J/kg. The gravity paragraph also still places him at the surface (crush radius from surface granite).
confirmed.evidence: State {"group":"solo","action":"weight","m":1e22}: verdict 'He sinks to the centre'; tiles 'Earth falls onto him in 14.9 min / free fall from the surface' and 'Energy released, at least 6.3 x 10^29 J'. m*(0 - premPhi(0)) = 1e22 x 4.916e7 = 4.9e29 J.
confirmed.fix: Show tff only for earthFalls and blackHole. For reshapes show 'sinks to the centre' and use m*(Phi_surface - Phi_centre) as the floor. Suppress or relabel the surface-based dBeat and crush-radius sentences.

verdict.title: 'Reshapes' regime still shows 'Earth falls onto him in 14.9 min' and an overstated energy floor
verdict.reason: Reproduced at m=1e22. The verdict says 'He sinks to the centre', but the tiles show 'Earth falls onto him in 14.9 min / free fall from the surface' (app.html:1464 shows tff for any regime but 'none') and 'Energy released, at least 6.3 x 10^29 J' (G m M_E/R_E). The guaranteed part, sinking from the surface to the centre, is m*(0 - premPhi(0)) = 1e22 x 4.916e7 = 4.9e29 J. The gravity paragraph still uses surface granite ('bedrock stays put unless it is within 1,060 km'). Density critique item 12 asked for tff to be dropped for reshapes and flagged rCrush. verdict.fix: Show the tff tile only for earthFalls and blackHole. For reshapes, show 'sinks to the centre' and use m*(Phi_surface - Phi_centre) as the 'at least' floor, or label the G m M_E/R_E figure as an estimate. confirmed.title: White-dwarf stop range shows '0 mm' because a run that never gets stuck defaults to r = 0
confirmed.claim: stuckRange maps any weak or strong rock run that doesn't get stuck to r = 0. With sigma = 0.1 GPa the white-dwarf run passes through the centre and turns ~112 km beyond it on its first pass, so it is never stuck. The page then prints 'anywhere from 0 mm to 646 km from the centre'. The static rest radius for 0.1 GPa is ~16 km. The calibration check 'rMin < 50 km' passes only because of this fallback.
confirmed.evidence: node: P.fallThrough(P.makeBody({H:2,m:4.986e8}), {sigma:0.1e9,k:0.5}) gives stuck null and firstPass.r 111,760 m. Bisecting (m - rho V) g(r) = sigma A for 0.1 GPa gives 16.5 km. An independent 1-D radial integration with weak rock passes the centre at ~2,670 m/s. Page {"group":"solo","action":"weight","m":498600000} says '(anywhere from 0 mm to 646 km from the centre ...)'. The 1.7 GPa and 4.1 GPa cases reproduce: 216 km at 6,792 s and 646 km.
confirmed.fix: For a run that doesn't stick, integrate with full:true until stuck, or use the static radius from settle()'s bisection. Word it as 'near the centre (~16 km)'.

verdict.title: White-dwarf stop range shows '0 mm' because a run that never gets stuck defaults to r = 0
verdict.reason: Reproduced at the current default height. The white-dwarf preset (3.05 m, 1.765e9 kg) prints 'about 87.3 km from the centre ... (anywhere from 0 mm to 394 km ...)'. At H=2 m, m=4.986e8 the page prints '0 mm to 646 km'. With sigma 0.1 GPa, fallThrough returns stuck=null and firstPass.r = 184 km (3.05 m) / 112 km (2 m), and stuckRange maps that to 0. The static rest radius from settle's bisection at 0.1 GPa is 10.8 km (3.05 m) and 16.5 km (2 m). Calibration line 154 ('rMin < 50e3') passes only because of this fallback. The finder's mass of 498,600,000 is the white-dwarf density only at 2 m. At the current default it reads as 7.8e8 kg/m^3 and shows 18.2 km, but the bug reproduces with the real preset.
verdict.fix: For a weak-rock run that doesn't stick on its first pass, use settle()'s static rStop for that sigma (or integrate with full:true until stuck). Word the range as 'from about 11 km to 394 km'. Tighten the calibration check to expect the static radius.

confirmed.title: Neutron-star matter caveat and its 3 x 10^32 Pa are applied far beyond neutron-star densities
confirmed.claim: The caveat appears for any rho >= 1e17 kg/m^3 and says 'Neutron-star matter stays this dense only under a neutron star's gravity, at a pressure of about 3 x 10^32 Pa'. That pressure belongs to nuclear density (~2.7e17). Neutron-star cores reach only about 1-3e18 kg/m^3. At 1e18 kg (5.6e18 kg/m^3) and 1e22 kg (5.6e22 kg/m^3) Rex is denser than any neutron star, and at 5.6e22 a degenerate-neutron estimate gives ~1e40 Pa. 'At least 16 MeV per neutron' remains a valid floor but is ~1,000x low there.
confirmed.evidence: State {"group":"solo","action":"weight","m":1e22} prints the neutron-star sentence with 3 x 10^32 Pa. Ultra-relativistic Fermi gas at n = rho/m_n = 3.3e49 m^-3: p_F c ~ 20 GeV; P ~ (ħc/4)(3π^2)^(1/3) n^(4/3) ~ 2.6e40 Pa.
confirmed.fix: Use the neutron-star wording only for about 1e17-2e18 kg/m^3. Above that say 'denser than any known matter, even neutron-star cores; the pressure holding it would be far higher', and keep 16 MeV as 'at least'.

verdict.title: Neutron-star matter caveat and its 3 x 10^32 Pa are applied far beyond neutron-star densities
verdict.reason: Reproduced at m=1e22 (rho 1.6e22 kg/m^3). The page says 'Neutron-star matter stays this dense only under a neutron star's gravity, at a pressure of about 3 x 10^32 Pa'. W8.P_NM is 2.2-3.4e32 Pa, the pressure of neutron matter at nuclear density, and the caveat fires for any rho >= 1e17. Neutron-star cores reach only ~1e18 kg/m^3, so at 1.6e22 no neutron star is this dense. An ultra-relativistic Fermi-gas estimate gives ~5e39 Pa, ~1e7 times the quoted figure. '16 MeV per neutron' remains a valid but very loose floor.
verdict.fix: Use the neutron-star sentence only for about 1e17-2e18 kg/m^3. Above that, say he is denser than any known matter, including neutron-star cores, and that the pressure needed would be far higher than 3 x 10^32 Pa. Keep 16 MeV per neutron as 'at least'.

confirmed.title: 'Twist on each upper arm' shows the winner's torque for both arms
confirmed.claim: The tile prints max(torqueA, torqueB) and labels it 'each'. During a pin the loser's humerus carries only his own muscle torque; the rest of the winner's surplus goes into spinning the forearms. verdict.title: Dense thrower 'can't even hold it up (2.18 PN)': the figure is his own arm's weight, and two pulls at right angles are added as scalars

confirmed.title: Fastball aims with interpolated release speeds that are up to 190x too high near vertical
confirmed.claim: releaseTable samples the full-strength speed every 7.5 degrees and interpolates linearly. Between 82.5 and 90 degrees the real speed is far from linear. On yielding ground the throw is footing-limited at every angle except exactly 90 degrees, where the footing limit becomes infinite (see the 89/90 finding). aimHard tries 89 degrees and gets a speed interpolated toward the 90-degree value. The result is false 'leaves Earth for good' and false 'fireball' verdicts for heavy objects at high strength. 31 of 567 heavy-object fastball legs change outcome when the speed is computed exactly. The grid was piano to pyramid, 10^6 to 10^22 kg, 10 m to 10,000 km.
confirmed.evidence: State {"group":"duo","duoAction":"catch","cObj":"pyramid","cLogD":5,"cStyle":"hard","logKg":20.5,"H":2,"m":180,"oH":2,"oM":180}. The page says: 'Thrown as hard as Rex can, the pyramid can't come down on Ollie: kept low, it burns its speed in the air; aimed higher, it leaves Earth for good.' The engine picks 89 degrees with vL 646,595 m/s. throwObject at 89 degrees gives 7,296 m/s. Pyramid at 10^19 kg: vOf(84) is 26,670 m/s in the table but 217 m/s directly (123x). vOf(86) is 61,990 vs 323 (192x). State {..."cObj":"eiffel","cLogD":5,"cStyle":"hard","logKg":20}. The page says: 'At 179,000 m/s · 645,000 km/h the tower turns into a fireball ... Past 1% of light speed the air can't get out of the way'. But 179 km/s is 0.06% of c. aimHard saw an interpolated speed at or above V_FIREBALL near 89 degrees, and leg (line 2394) then reports tab.vOf(0). With exact speeds both legs are 'too-weak'. All of this was reproduced on the 01:29 build.
confirmed.fix: Compute vOf exactly (memoize throwObject(noFl, obj, th) per angle), or add table points at 84, 86, 88, 89, 89.5 and 89.9 degrees and interpolate log v. In the aimHard/leg fireball branch, report the speed of the angle that triggered it, and only take the branch when that throw really reaches 1% of c.

verdict.title: Fastball aims with interpolated release speeds that are up to 190x too high near vertical
verdict.reason: Reproduced. One caveat about the evidence: the state as written (H 2, m 180, no build 'human') is migrated on load to the default 3.048 m bodies (app.html line 567). So the first quoted pyramid text does not appear at logKg 20.5. With default bodies the page instead says 'too big' at 1,450 m/s. The bug itself is real on the shipped page. (1) Eiffel, logKg 20, 100 km, Fastball: the page says 'At 283,000 m/s ... the tower turns into a fireball ... Past 1% of light speed the air can't get out of the way'. 283 km/s is 0.094% of c. (2) Eiffel, logKg 19: the page says 'At 40,800 m/s ... turns into a fireball', which is 0.014% of c. (3) Pyramid, logKg 18, 100 km: the page says '... aimed higher, it leaves Earth for good'. With exact speeds this is 'too-weak'. With the human calibration bodies the engine gives vL 646,595 m/s at 89 degrees. throwObject gives 7,296 m/s at that angle, so the table is 89x too high. I patched a scratch copy of engine.js so vOf calls throwObject exactly (memoized). Over 11 heavy objects x 17 strengths x 7 distances with default bodies, 74 of 1,309 Fastball legs change outcome: false 'too-big', false 'overshoots: escapes' and false 'fireball'. The second part of the claim holds even with exact speeds. 14 legs still report a fireball at a speed below 1% of c. aimHard returns fireball as soon as any grid angle, here the near-vertical 89 degrees, reaches V_FIREBALL. leg (line 2394) then prints tab.vOf(0) and says the fireball 'keeps rushing toward' Ollie, though the throw that triggered it goes almost straight up. Not covered by the earlier critiques.
verdict.fix: Compute vOf exactly per angle (memoize throwObject(noFl, obj, th)), or add table points at 84, 86, 88, 89, 89.5 and 89.9 degrees and interpolate log v. Interpolating log v alone still misleads because of the 1/cos footing singularity, so exact values are safer. Separately, in aimHard do not return 'fireball' just because some steep angle reaches 1% of c. Return it only when the flattest angle whose path would reach Ollie needs or uses a speed of at least 1% of c, and report that angle's own speed and direction. A near-vertical relativistic throw should read as 'goes up, not toward him', not as a fireball rushing at Ollie.

confirmed.title: Gentle lob says no landing arc exists at 10,000 km when one does
confirmed.claim: aimEasy counts escaping or orbiting flights as 'reaching' so the speed search stays monotone. It then takes the minimum speed over all angles. At steep angles, escape needs less speed than a landing arc at 60 to 65 degrees. So it picks an escaping 85-degree throw, and leg returns 'no-arc'. The page then states as fact that every throw fast enough goes into orbit or escapes.
confirmed.evidence: State {"group":"duo","duoAction":"catch","cObj":"tank","cLogD":7,"cStyle":"easy","logKg":16,"groundHolds":true,"H":2,"m":180,"oH":2,"oM":180}. The page says: 'No thrown arc comes down 10,000 km away: anything fast enough to get there goes into orbit or leaves the Earth...' The engine picks 85.0 degrees at 550,600 m/s, which escapes. flyTo finds landing arcs at 60 degrees (847,000 m/s, lands at 10,004 km) and 65 degrees (769,000 m/s, lands at 10,078 km). Rex's full-strength speed at 60 to 65 degrees is 1.26e6 m/s. The same false 'no-arc' shows for loco, shuttle, Titanic, Nimitz and Ruyi staff at 10,000 km. Those arcs may well burn up, but the stated reason is false.
confirmed.fix: Minimise only over speeds whose flight lands. Keep the overshoot shortcut only inside each angle's bisection. Return 'no-arc' only when no angle has a landing solution, and let the heat and break-up gates judge the landing arc.

verdict.title: Gentle lob says no landing arc exists at 10,000 km when one does
verdict.reason: Reproduced. Tank, 10,000 km, Gentle lob, logKg 16, comic ground: the page says 'No thrown arc comes down 10,000 km away: anything fast enough to get there goes into orbit or leaves the Earth, unless it skims the whole way through the air, which no object survives.' The engine picks 85.0 degrees at 550,379 m/s, which escapes. Direct flyTo finds arcs that land past Dfl: 45 degrees at 2.0e6 m/s, 55 degrees at 1.05e6, 60 degrees at 8.7e5 and 65 degrees at 7.9e5 m/s. The air slows the tank to about 10 km/s, and it then flies a suborbital arc. All are below Rex's 1.55e6 m/s at 60 to 65 degrees. A scan of every catalog object found the same false 'no-arc' for tank, loco, shuttle, Titanic, Nimitz, ESB and Ruyi at 10,000 km or the antipode. I downgraded this to minor because every such landing arc needs a launch ram pressure 20 to 270,000 times the object's crush strength. With a correct aim the result becomes 'breaks-up', so the bottom line (no catch, stand closer) is unchanged. Only the stated reason is false. No catalog object is indestructible, so no reader-visible catch is lost.
verdict.fix: In aimEasy, minimise launch speed only over flights that actually land at D. Keep counting overshoots as 'reaching' only inside each angle's bisection, for monotonicity. Return 'no-arc' only when no angle lands, and let the break-up and burn-up gates judge the landing arc, so the page says why it fails.

confirmed.title: Render times near or over 2 s in Catch and Shove
confirmed.claim: Some reachable states block the main thread for 1 to 2.5 s per render on a desktop, and slider drags re-render every 180 ms. Catch lobs of heavy objects at 10 to 100 km are the worst, especially when Rex and Ollie differ, because two legs are computed. Each leg runs 8 angles plus a golden-section search, with an 80-step bisection of full flights at each angle. Shove 'both at once' with very heavy bodies is slow in shoveOnce/pushApart.
confirmed.evidence: In-page renderBay times (Chromium, 4 cores, load about 2). Catch with {"cObj":"b777","cLogD":4,"cStyle":"easy","logKg":12,"H":0.1,"m":0.0225,"oH":500,"oM":2.8125e9} took 1,882 ms. Catch with {"cObj":"eiffel","cLogD":5,"cStyle":"easy","logKg":12,"H":2,"m":180,"oH":2,"oM":180} took 1,050 ms. Wrestle with {"wrestleMove":"shove","wrestleWho":"both","logKg":34,"H":2,"m":1e21,"oH":2,"oM":1e21,"oAnchor":"bolted"} took 2,435 ms. In node, catchGame over 4,968 states (4 size pairs x 23 objects x 9 distances x 3 strengths x 2 styles) had 220 over 1 s, 14 over 2 s and a maximum of 2.9 s.

verdict.title: Render times near or over 2 s in Catch and Shove
verdict.reason: Reproduced. Node timings with load about 2: the b777 lob with unequal bodies (two legs) took 2.86 s. Eiffel lob at 100 km took 0.9 s per leg (1.79 s for two). shoveBoth with 1e21 kg bodies at logKg 34 took 2.2 s. Chromium page loads for the same states took 2.6 s, 1.7 s and 2.2 s, against 0.54 s for the default page. One small misstatement: the distance slider is debounced (scheduleBaySlow clears its timer on each input), so it re-renders after a 180 ms pause, not every 180 ms during a drag. Each pause still freezes the page for 1 to 3 s. The strength dial's 30 ms debounce makes this worse when it is dragged on these tabs.

verdict.title: Weight tab jumps from 4.89 m deep to the inner core over a 0.03% mass change (500 m Rex)

verdict.title: Solo Throw: launch angle 89 to 90 degrees changes the throw about 100x (root of the catch interpolation error)
verdict.reason: Reproduced with default bodies, pyramid, logKg 19. At 88 degrees: 1,500 m/s, Rex shoved back at 5.71% c. At 89 degrees: 2,990 m/s, flies 28.6 km, Rex shoved back at 2.86% c. At 90 degrees: 164,000 m/s, leaves Earth. R2 = (mu Nmax + dig)/cos(theta) + ... is a 1/cos singularity and goes infinite only when cos < 1e-9. It is pre-existing, not a regression, and the page explains the 89-degree footing limit. It matters mainly because it drives finding 1. The proposed fix is too weak, though. Passive lateral rock resistance is at most about sigma x a few m^2, around 1e10 N, far below the 5.8e17 N sideways load at 89 degrees, so adding it would not remove the cliff. The real inconsistency is at 90 degrees. There the model lets the failing ground carry an unlimited vertical reaction ('sinks but is not freed'), while at 89 degrees it caps the sideways part at mu Nmax.
verdict.fix: In the catch, stop interpolating toward the singular 90-degree value: use exact per-angle speeds, or cap the table at 89.x degrees. For the solo throw, treat the two axes the same way. When bearing fails by orders of magnitude, the vertical reaction isn't fully resisted either, so he should be driven into the ground, as in Weight/fallThrough. Alternatively, state on the page that the vertical throw assumes the planet takes the reaction.

confirmed.title: Neutron-matter caveat applies ρ₀-only facts from 10¹⁷ kg/m³ up, with a false 'at least 16 MeV' bound
confirmed.claim: The caveat appears whenever ρ ≥ 1e17 kg/m³ (engine.js:922). It always says 'at a pressure of about 3 × 10³² Pa' and 'giving up at least 16 MeV per neutron'. Facts neutron_star_matter_pressure_saturation and neutron_matter_energy_per_particle give these values only at saturation density ρ₀ = 2.7e17 kg/m³. Below ρ₀ both numbers are lower, and at the 1.53 ρ₀ neutron-star preset the pressure is higher. Even at ρ₀, Hebeler et al. give 16.3 ± 2.2 MeV, so 'at least 16' contradicts the source's own range (14.1–18.5). The density critique asked for this fix and it has not been made. nuclear_saturation_density.notes still states the 1e17 threshold.
confirmed.evidence: State {group:'solo',action:'weight',H:2,m:2.7e16,groundHolds:true} gives ρ = 1.5e17 = 0.56 ρ₀. The page prints: 'Neutron-star matter stays this dense only under a neutron star's gravity, at a pressure of about 3 × 10³² Pa. Freed, it expands violently ... giving up at least 16 MeV per neutron (about 370 kt of TNT per kilogram).' The Hebeler PDF (arXiv:1007.1746, fetched) has 'En(ρ0)/N = 16.3 ± 2.2 MeV' and 'P(ρ0) = 1.4 − 2.1 MeV fm−3', both stated at ρ0 = 2.7 × 10^14 g cm−3.
confirmed.fix: Show the caveat only for ρ ≥ ρ₀ (2.7e17), or reword it below ρ₀. Write 'about 14–19 MeV per neutron at nuclear density (more when denser)' and 'at least about 2–3 × 10³² Pa'. Update the 1e17 note in nuclear_saturation_density, and the '>= 16 MeV' comment at engine.js:656.

verdict.title: Neutron-matter caveat applies ρ₀-only facts from 10¹⁷ kg/m³ up, with a false 'at least 16 MeV' bound
verdict.reason: Reproduced. With H 2, m 2.7e16 and comic ground (ρ = 1.5e17 = 0.56 ρ₀), the page prints the caveat with 'about 3 × 10³² Pa' and 'at least 16 MeV per neutron'. The gate is ρ ≥ 1e17 (engine.js:922). Both numbers are Hebeler's values at ρ₀ only. The density critique flagged this and it was not fixed. Two caveats on the finder's claim. First, the presets sit above ρ₀ (neutron star 4.12e17 = 1.53 ρ₀), where the energy statement is closer to right and the pressure is understated rather than overstated. Second, 'at least' is not plainly false. The fact's own notes say later beta decays and nuclear reactions add more (forming nuclei adds roughly 8 MeV per nucleon), so the total yield likely exceeds 16 MeV even at 14.1 MeV for E/N. But no cited fact supports that bound, and the J figure uses exactly 16.3 MeV. It only affects custom densities between 1e17 and 2.7e17 and the pressure wording, so minor, not major.
verdict.fix: Gate the caveat at ρ ≥ ρ₀ (2.7e17), or reword it below ρ₀. Say 'at nuclear density, a pressure of about 2–3 × 10³² Pa (more when denser)' and '16 ± 2 MeV per neutron at nuclear density, with more from the nuclei that form and decay afterwards'. Update the nuclear_saturation_density note and the engine.js:656 comment.

Quake: 1 part in 10,000 of Q, upper bound.' Card text: 'Quake magnitudes assume 1 part in 10,000 ... (real range 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³, so give or take about ⅔ of a magnitude)'.

verdict.title: Collide math labels the quake an 'upper bound'; the card and engine treat it as a middle estimate
verdict.reason: Reproduced. A collide run at a set speed into bolted Rex prints 'Quake: 1 part in 10,000 of Q, upper bound.' The assumption card says quakes are a middle estimate, give or take ⅔ of a magnitude. The finder misreads the engine comment, though. 'upper bound: as if all of it went into the ground' means all of Q is treated as ground-impact energy, which then gets the 1e-4 share. That is consistent and not false. The upper-bound part is the energy input, not the seismic share. The page line still reads as if the magnitude were an upper bound, which it is not, because the share can be 10× higher. It is a label inconsistency, so minor.
verdict.fix: Use 'Quake: 1 part in 10,000 of Q (the usual share, give or take ⅔ of a magnitude), as if all of Q reached the ground, which overstates it'. The engine comment can stay; optionally clarify it as 'energy input upper bound; seismic share is the middle value'.

confirmed.title: Catch survival gate uses 'grip limit' estimates as whole-object crush and break-up strength
confirmed.claim: Break-up in flight (ρv² > obj.crush), 'wreckage' (stopping force / obj.area > obj.crush) and break-at-launch all use obj.crush (engine.js:2282, 2426, 2430, 2432). In the data, obj.crush is the 'Grip limit (estimate)'. build-data.py:188-189 defines it as 'Contact pressure a hand-sized grip can apply before the structure gives way locally ... thin skins give far below the material's yield strength'. That is a local, thin-skin value, not a bulk strength for tearing apart or crushing the whole object. Fact catch_breakup_ram_pressure says it uses 'the crush strengths already in its object list', but the object list has no crush strengths. The page calls 3 MPa 'what it can take', and no row in the sources table is named 'crush strength'. 'Its whole front' is also the orientation-averaged tumbling area: 8.7 m² for a Corolla, printed as 2.95 m × 2.95 m.
confirmed.evidence: Catch tab, car fastball, logKg 10: 'The air tears it apart the moment it leaves Rex's hand: it pushes on its front with up to 44.4 MPa, past the ~3 MPa it can take.' At logKg 8 with Rex bolted: 'Even spread over its whole front (2.95 m × 2.95 m) ... 8.9× the ~3 MPa it can take.' Show the math: 'Break-up in flight: ρ v² > its crush strength (as in Collins et al. 2005 ...); here up to 1.44 MPa against 3 MPa.' Sources table: 'Grip limit (estimate): Toyota Corolla | 3 MPa'.
confirmed.fix: Either add sourced or estimated bulk break-up strengths per object as a separate field and fact, or relabel these values on the page as 'its grip limit (a rough estimate of local crushing)' and mark the break-up and wreckage verdicts as rough. Call the tumbling area 'its average cross-section', not 'its whole front'.

verdict.title: Catch survival gate uses 'grip limit' estimates as whole-object crush and break-up strength
verdict.reason: Reproduced. The break-up (engine.js:2426/2432) and wreckage (2430, wholeFront = F/obj.area/obj.crush) checks both use obj.crush. The sources table labels that field 'Grip limit (estimate)', defined as local contact pressure under a hand-sized grip (build-data.py:188-189). The page calls it 'its crush strength' and 'the ~3 MPa it can take', with no row of that name. obj.area for the Corolla is the 8.7 m² orientation-averaged area, printed as 'its whole front (2.95 m × 2.95 m)', wider and taller than the car. Both choices make the gate lenient. With logKg 7 and Ollie bolted, the page says 'Stopping it in 91 cm takes 24.5 MN. His palms punch into it… 1,800 g on the car' and reports a catch, not a wreck, because 24.5 MN < 3 MPa × 8.7 m². In the logKg 8 bolted case, the car survives flight at 1.44 MPa (about 14 atm) ram pressure. Real car structures crush at well under 1 MN, and panels fail far below 3 MPa, so the verdicts err toward survival.
verdict.fix: Add a separate, labelled estimate of bulk break-up and crush strength for each object (for vehicles, a crash-structure crush force or a pressure well below the grip limit), or relabel the page wording as 'its grip limit (a rough local value)' and mark these verdicts as rough. Use the real frontal area, not the tumbling average, for the 'whole front' check, or call it 'its average cross-section'. Correct the catch_breakup_ram_pressure note.

confirmed.title: Run rule (strength > weight) contradicts the cited running force; walk rule mixes one-leg and two-leg forces
confirmed.claim: moveCheck sets run: F > W, which means both legs push only 1.4 W. The fact the page cites, walking_running_peak_vertical_force (Nilsson & Thorstensson 1989), gives running peaks of 2.0–2.9 body weights per stance. The walk rule compares 1.4F (the two-leg jump force) with 1.2 W, which the card at static-data.js:24 calls the load 'on one leg'. The density critique flagged this and it has not been fixed.
confirmed.evidence: Current default body (3.05 m, 637 kg), weight tab, logKg 2.8169: chip 'Can walk and run' with tile 'strength is 1.03× his weight'. His legs push 1.4 × 1.03 = 1.44 W, below the source's 2.0–2.9 b.w. running range. Show the math: 'Walk: ≥ 1.2 W (Nilsson & Thorstensson 1989). Run (Sprint tab): strength > W.'
confirmed.fix: Use one per-leg basis. Either one leg = 0.7F, so walk needs 0.7F ≥ 1.2 W and run needs 0.7F ≥ 2.0–2.9 W, or state the two-leg basis explicitly and set run at 1.4F ≥ 2.5 W, matching sprint()'s own per-stance assumption. Say on the page which one is used.

verdict.title: Run rule (strength > weight) contradicts the cited running force; walk rule mixes one-leg and two-leg forces
verdict.reason: Reproduced. At logKg 2.8169 with the default body, the chip says 'Can walk and run' at 1.03× weight. The walk bullet compares the two-leg 1.4F with a one-leg load of 1.2 W ('he has 7.4× that'), mixing bases, and the density critique's fix was not applied. But the run rule is the Sprint tab's own gate (sprint() returns 'too weak' unless F > W), and the page says 'Run (Sprint tab)'. It does not cite Nilsson & Thorstensson for running. The finder's per-leg fix is wrong. With 0.7F ≥ 2.0 W, the calibration body (511 kg lift, 180 kg: F/W 2.84, 0.7F = 1.99 W) could not run, though it reproduces Bolt's top speed. With 1.4F ≥ 2.5 W, an ordinary man deadlifting 1.2× body weight could not run. Force-plate peaks come from near-straight, elastic legs, so a deadlift-based dial does not map onto them directly. The real defect is the mixed-basis wording, which is labelled a 'rough rule', so minor.
verdict.fix: Keep the Sprint tab's rule but state the basis plainly: 'both legs push up to 1.4× the dial; walking puts about 1.2× his weight on one leg; running uses the Sprint tab's rough rule (strength above his weight); running peaks of 2–2.9 body weights per stance come from near-straight, springy legs, which the dial doesn't model'. Don't adopt 0.7F ≥ 2–2.9 W, which breaks the calibration.

verdict.title: Ostriker gravitational drag drives the headline settle time but has no research fact or source row
verdict.reason: Reproduced. No research JSON or sources-table row mentions Ostriker. It appears only in the card, the math line and engine comments. Scratch copies with CS_ROCK 3000/6000/9000/13000 give settle(7.416e16 kg, 2 m) = 44.5/125.9/231.0/400 years, and DF_LNL 3–10 changes nothing (the late, subsonic swings dominate, where I ≈ M³/3). Realistic deep-Earth sound speeds (S 4.5–7, P 8–13.7 km/s) mostly push the time up, inside the stated 81–29,000 years. Only c_s below about 4.5 km/s falls under the minimum. The gap is traceability, not a wrong headline.

verdict.title: Lift tile shows the contact-path gravity peak but labels it with the overhead distance
verdict.reason: Reproduced. liftPartner gives Fg = 9.15e-6 N at the default body. G·637²/2.286² = 5.18e-6 N, while 0.385·G·637²/1.068² = 9.15e-6 N. verdict.title: Default Push and Arm views: the chips contradict the verdict and the math
verdict.reason: All three reproduce in default states. (1) Collide > Push: the verdict says 'Dead heat... Neither moves. Both are pushing as hard as their feet allow', next to the chip 'Ollie’s feet slip first'. The chip comes from pusherSlips = F > RA, so it means 'footing, not strength, is his limit', but it reads as if he slips. (2) Arm: the chip 'Arm force: Rex 3.75 kN · Ollie 3.75 kN' shows the footing-capped value. The bars ('Rex’s arm 222 kN') and the math ('Arm force = 25% of strength: Rex 222 kN') use 'arm force' for 222 kN. (3) Catch: the prose says the squash is 'about 3 cm to 7.6 cm (an estimate)', while the math at app.html:2043 hard-codes 'over a 2–5 cm squash'. That is the 2 m value. The engine uses GIVE_LO/HI × H, which is 3.05–7.6 cm at the default 3.05 m. These are label mismatches, not wrong physics, so minor.

The engine’s holdNeeded is his arm weight (1e12 kg × arm share × g). {"cObj":"car","cStyle":"hard","logKg":8}: arrival 'level', bullet 'The more it presses him down, the harder his feet grip, so his arms push 73 MN.'

verdict.title: Catch text misstates the forces: 'His arms can stop it: 2.8%' and 'he can’t even hold it [the baseball] up (29.5 GN)'
verdict.reason: Partly real. Part (a) is refuted. The bowling-ball chip 'His arms can stop it: 2.8% of Ollie’s strength' is k.Fpeak/Fcap for the arm stroke (25.3 kN / 890 kN). In the catch model (the catchIt first-contact step that the catch critique asked for), the 1.23–3.07 MN first hit is taken by the inertia of his 28 kg hands and forearms, not by his muscles. The page says so in its bullet ('most of it happens in the first instant... His arms then bring it in over 91 cm with 25.3 kN'). Comparing F1 with his strength, as the suggested fix does, would compare unlike quantities. Part (b) is real. With m=oM=1e12, logKg 8 and both bolted, the page says 'Rex can’t throw the baseball: he can’t even hold it up (29.5 GN)'. holdNeeded = (obj.m + armMass)·g + obj.m·gSelf (engine.js:1037). That is about 3e9 kg of his own super-dense arm, while the ball adds about 10 N. The Arm tab words the same case correctly ('can’t even hold his forearm up'). Part (c) is real. For a level car fastball (logKg 8), the bullet says 'The more it presses him down, the harder his feet grip, so his arms push 73 MN'. At θ=0, anchorCapacity’s N(F) does not depend on F, and the 73 MN comes from inertia (F/mS + F/Mb = v²/2d).
verdict.fix: Keep the '% of strength' chip as is, but its label could read 'His arms then stop it: 2.8%...'. For cant-hold, write 'Rex can’t even hold his own hand and forearm up at this density (29.5 GN)' when armMass·g dominates holdNeeded. Print the 'presses him down' sentence only when the arrival angle is meaningfully downward (sin γ·F is not negligible next to M g). Otherwise say 'He skids while he stops it; his arms push 73 MN because the car and he share the stopping.'

verdict.title: Wrestle and catch text ignores the chosen setting or the outcome
verdict.reason: All sub-claims reproduced. (1) Partner Fastball: tossPartner uses v = vMax when style !== 'easy' (engine.js:2463) and ignores hTarget. The slider label still reads 'Toss height: 10 m', and moving it (cLogD) changes nothing; the verdict is 'tosses Ollie 95.1 m up' either way. The 'Show what happens if he misses' box is shown, but catchPartner never reads it. (2) Shove 'Both at once' prints the same one-way text as Rex → Ollie ('Ollie flies back... slides 76.5 m... Rex recoils at 32.2 m/s'), with only an 'Ollie slides' tile, for equal bodies. (3) A failed lift (oM 1e9) says 'Rex can’t lift Ollie...' and then 'The ground under Rex carries both of them: 46.9 GPa'. Hide the miss checkbox there. For 'both', describe both partners sliding and add a tile for each. Print the ground-load bullet only on a successful lift. Drop the slide and landing bullets when the speed reaches the fireball threshold or the body escapes or orbits.

verdict.title: Catch tab leaves out the thrower’s recoil that the Throw tab reports for the same throw
verdict.reason: Reproduced, and the critiques don’t cover it. Car fastball at logKg 8: Catch says 'Rex fires the car at 602 m/s', with nothing about Rex. Throw (angle 0) says 'Rex gets shoved backward at 1,270 m/s', and 'He ends up with more of the energy than the car does'. Shuttle at logKg 10: Catch says 'fires the shuttle stack at 4.96 m/s'. Throw shows a 15,500 m/s recoil, which is above escape speed, so Rex would leave the planet. The Catch tab still quotes a round-trip time that assumes both partners stand still. catchLeg returns no recoil field, and the catch bay (app.html:1966–1998) only shows the catcher’s slide.
verdict.fix: Carry throwObject’s recoil (the thrower’s speed and slide) through leg(). Add a tile or bullet such as 'Rex is shoved back at 1,270 m/s and slides X'. When the thrower’s slide exceeds the gap, or his recoil exceeds escape speed, drop the round trip or flag it ('they don’t stay in range for a second throw').

confirmed.title: Badly formatted numbers across the Weight, Catch, Arm and Collide tabs
confirmed.claim: The page prints huge percentages, long m/s and g digit strings, a 0 mm range end, fractional '×' ratios, an '∞' radius, a meaningless Mach number, and '≈' for a 40% gap. This goes against the owner’s plain-number preference.

White dwarf: '(anywhere from 0 mm to 394 km from the centre'; '21 Mt TNT · ≈ Castle Bravo' (15 Mt). Catch {"cStyle":"hard","logKg":12}: 'fires the baseball at 1,490,000 m/s (Mach 4,400)'. Catch real-muscle human: 'squeezes the ball 0.083–0.21× as hard'. Arm real: '0.083× what the table top is built to take'. Collide light speed: 'Rock cracks ∞ around his bolts', '0.0033 ns'. Weight weak: 'strength is 2 × 10⁻³ of his weight'. Lob chip: 'Nose air 15 °C: warms up' (nothing warms at 8.9 m/s).

verdict.title: Badly formatted numbers across the Weight, Catch, Arm and Collide tabs
verdict.reason: Most examples reproduce. m=1e25: '6,300,000,000% of the energy it takes to blow the Earth apart' and 'Gravity at his skin 240,000,000,000,000 g'. m=1e22: 'Escape speed from him 1,580,000 m/s'. White dwarf: '(anywhere from 0 mm to 394 km from the centre' and '21 Mt TNT · ≈ Castle Bravo'; compareEnergy uses '≈' up to a ratio of 1.5, and Castle Bravo is 15 Mt. Catch fastball at logKg 12: '1,490,000 m/s (Mach 4,400)'. Collide: 'Rock cracks ∞' and '0.0033 ns'. Default lob: 'Nose air 15 °C: warms up'. fmtRatio (app.html:521) has no branch below 1, so values like '0.083×' can appear. I didn’t hit those exact states with my guesses for the 'real human' state keys. These are presentation problems, not wrong physics.
verdict.fix: Above 100%, write N× ('63 million× the energy'). Use km/s above 10 km/s, and scientific notation for g above 1e6. Write 'at the centre' for a lower bound of 0. Give fmtRatio a '%' branch below 1. Skip Mach above about Mach 50 or 1% of light speed. Use '≈' only within ±15%, and say '1.4× Castle Bravo' otherwise. Use ps below 1 ns. Hide the nose-air chip when the heating is under about 5 °C.

verdict.reason: Reproduced at 390 px (2× screenshots in audit/sk-ux/cut-light.png, cut-dark.png and bars.png).
